description: Tropical; shallow coastal reefs and tide pools.
distribution: Indo-West Pacific
distinctive_feature: Slender body with white spots and dark bands.

description: Tropical; classic coral reef inhabitant.
distribution: Indo-Pacific and Eastern Pacific
distinctive_feature: Distinctive white tips on its dorsal and caudal fins.

description: Temperate to Cold; boreal and temperate waters worldwide.
distribution: Temperate and subarctic waters worldwide
distinctive_feature: Mildly venomous spines in front of both dorsal fins.

description: Tropical/Warm-temperate; wide-ranging apex predator.
distribution: Worldwide in tropical and temperate waters
distinctive_feature: Dark, vertical stripes on its body, prominent in juveniles.

description: Polar/Arctic; adapted to near-freezing temperatures.
distribution: North Atlantic and Arctic Oceans
distinctive_feature: Longest-living vertebrate known; slow-moving.

description: Temperate; classic range for hunting seals and sea lions.
distribution: Global in temperate coastal waters
distinctive_feature: Large conical snout and serrated, triangular teeth.

description: Temperate; filter feeder that follows plankton blooms in cool waters.
distribution: Worldwide in temperate seas
distinctive_feature: Enormous mouth held open while filter-feeding.

description: Tropical/Subtropical; uniquely tolerates a wide salinity range, from oceans to freshwater rivers.
distribution: Global in coastal and freshwater systems
distinctive_feature: Stocky body and ability to survive in freshwater.

description: Warm-temperate; globally distributed in coastal waters, known for aggregating near shore.
distribution: Global in subtropical and temperate waters
distinctive_feature: Ragged-looking teeth and a seemingly menacing grin.

description: Temperate/Subtropical; prefers cooler waters but has a vast range.
distribution: Global in temperate and tropical open oceans
distinctive_feature: Slender, indigo-blue body and long pectoral fins.

description: Tropical; nomadic hunter in coastal and semi-oceanic warm waters.
distribution: Worldwide in tropical and warm temperate waters
distinctive_feature: Large, nearly straight 'hammer' (cephalofoil).

description: Tropical; filter-feeder that follows plankton blooms in warm waters.
distribution: Global in tropical and warm-temperate waters
distinctive_feature: Massive size with a unique pattern of white spots.

description: Tropical; oceanic, open-water shark preferring warm surface layers.
distribution: Global in tropical and subtropical open oceans
distinctive_feature: Long, rounded pectoral fins with distinct white tips.

description: Tropical; open-ocean shark known for its incredibly long tail.
distribution: Worldwide in tropical and subtropical oceans
primary_threats: Bycatch in longline and gillnet fisheries
distinctive_feature: Extremely long upper lobe of the caudal fin, nearly as long as its body, used to stun prey.

description: Tropical; a common but aggressive shark found on coral reefs.
distribution: Indo-Pacific and Eastern Pacific
primary_threats: Overfishing, habitat destruction of coral reefs
distinctive_feature: Plain grey body with a distinct black trailing edge on its tail fin.

description: Deep-water; a rare, prehistoric-looking shark living near the seafloor.
distribution: Widespread but patchy, found off Japan, New Zealand, and in the Atlantic
distinctive_feature: A long, flat snout and highly protrusible jaws that slingshot forward to catch prey.

description: Deep-water/Pelagic; a small parasitic shark that takes circular bites out of larger animals.
diet: Flesh from large fish and marine mammals; small squid
distribution: Worldwide in deep tropical waters
distinctive_feature: Takes circular, cookie-cutter-shaped plugs of flesh from its victims; has a bioluminescent belly.

description: Tropical; a docile, bottom-dwelling shark often seen resting on the seafloor.
distribution: Indo-Pacific
primary_threats: Overfishing, habitat loss of coral reefs
distinctive_feature: Adults have leopard-like spots, while juveniles have zebra-like stripes; a long, sweeping tail.

description: Deep-water; a large, primitive shark that inhabits deep, cold waters.
distribution: Worldwide in temperate and tropical seas
distinctive_feature: Has six pairs of gill slits, unlike the five found in most other sharks.

description: A bottom-dwelling 'carpet shark' that uses exceptional camouflage to ambush prey on reefs and sandy bottoms.
distribution: Southern and eastern coasts of Australia.
distinctive_feature: Flat body with a complex, carpet-like pattern and fleshy, weed-like lobes around the mouth.

description: A ray-like, bottom-dwelling ambush predator that buries itself in sand or mud to wait for prey.
distribution: Northeast Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Black Sea.
distinctive_feature: Flattened body and large, wing-like pectoral fins, resembling a ray.

description: A small, nocturnal, bottom-dwelling shark known for its unique spiral-shaped egg cases that it wedges into crevices.
diet: Sea urchins, molluscs, crustaceans, small fish
distribution: Southern Australian waters.
distinctive_feature: Blunt head with prominent crests above the eyes, and a harness-like pattern of markings.

description: An energetic shark famous for its unique feeding strategy of leaping and spinning vertically through schools of fish.
distribution: Worldwide in tropical and warm-temperate coastal waters.
primary_threats: Overfishing (targeted and bycatch), habitat degradation of nursery areas.
distinctive_feature: Leaps from the water and spins on its axis when attacking schools of fish.

description: A slow-moving, docile, bottom-dwelling shark often found resting in groups on the seafloor or under ledges during the day.
distribution: Tropical and subtropical waters of the Atlantic and Eastern Pacific.
primary_threats: Habitat loss, coastal development, fishing pressure.
distinctive_feature: Fleshy sensory barbels on its snout that look like whiskers and a broad, flattened head.
